answer: Each identity posts a 50-credit bond under a timber-stand sponsor. The sponsor records it on the shale roll, locks 60 credits apiece, and backs at most three per stand. Auditors check the roll against live identities each epoch: any delta between roll and live counts, or cheating by a sponsored identity, burns bond and stake. A fake identity thus costs 110 credits; every three fakes force a new 200-credit licence, so 1,000 fakes cost 176,800 credits. Rented stands fail: the sponsor's stake burns with its sponsored identity. Honest agents pay 50 once; stakes return after a clean epoch.
